caseno: Civil Appeal No. 328 of 2015 with Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2502 of 2013.

AM Aminuddin, Senior Advocate instructed by Md Zahirul Islam, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioner. (In CP No. 2502/13)

Rajdhani Unnayan Ka tripakkha (RAJUK) and others ------- Respondents (In CA No.328/15) Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Land and others ------- Respondents [in CP No.2502/13]
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 9-2-2011 passed by the High- Court Division in Writ Petition No. 7115 of 2009 and 4785 of 2007.)
full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique, J: These appeal and Civil Petition are directed against the judgment and order dated 9-2-2011 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 7115 of 2009 discharging the Rule.

2. The relevant facts, for the disposal of these appeal and Civil Petition, are that the appellants filed aforesaid writ petition challenging the inaction and failure of the writ-respondents by way of not mutating the names of the writ-petitioners pursuant to their application dated 24-8-2006 in the record of the RAJUK and also for a direction upon the respondents to mutate their names in its record.

3. The dispute is in respect of the land measuring an area of 1 (one) bigha and 8 chataks of Plot No. 11, Block NW(K), Road No. 50 of the layout plan of Gulshan Residential Model Town, Dhaka (hereinafter referred to as "the disputed property"). It was the case of the writ-petitioner that one Mostafa Haider got allotment of the disputed property from the then DIT (at present, the RAJUK) on the basis of deed of lease No. 9927 dated 13-10-1965. Mostafa Haider entered into an agreement for sale of the disputed property on 5-8-1971 with one KM Ataul Huq, predecessor-in-interest of the present appellants at a consideration of Taka 52,000 and upon receiving Taka 11,000 he executed the agreement. Thereafter, Mostafa Haider, receiving the rest consideration of Taka 41,000, executed a sale deed in December, 1971 in favour of KM Ataul Huq but the same was not registered. KM Ataul Huq sought permission from the RAJUK to get the sale deed registered but the RAJUK by its letter dated 07-7-1972 directed KM Ataul Huq to seek relief from the Court. Accordingly, Ataul Huq filed Title Suit No. 80 of 1975 (which was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 459 of 1985) in the First Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for Specific Performance of Contract. The RAJUK appeared in the said suit and contested the same by filing written statement. The trial Court dismissed the suit but, on appeal, the same was decreed in Title Appeal No. 51 of 1989. The RAJUK filed Civil Revision in the High Court Division and lost which was upheld by the Appellate Division as well. Thereafter, Ataul Huq filed Title Execution Case No. 7 of 1992 and got the sale deed registered through Court on 8-10-1992. Heirs of Ataul Huq, by filing the instant writ petition in the High Court Division, obtained Rule.

4. The writ-respondent Nos. 1 and 4 contested the writ petition by filing affidavit-in-opposition contending that the RAJUK lost the original "nothi" in respect of the disputed plot. It was further contended that the disputed plot was allotted to one Mostafa Haider on 2-9-1960 and he got the lease deed executed and registered on 9-10-1965. KM Ataul Huq himself applied for getting allotment of the disputed property in his name by filing an application on 15-3-1972 which was not considered. There-after, he filed a suit for Specific Performance of Contract. Meanwhile, the allotment order of the suit plot was cancelled since Mostafa Haider failed to construct of any structure in the same as per terms stipulated in the lease deed. The International Finance Investment and Commerce Bank Limited by a letter informed the RAJUK that Mostafa Haider took loan from the said bank of a sum of Taka 1 crore and 20 Lacs. The RAJUK informed the said bank that the clearance certificate allegedly issued by the RAJUK was fake, for which, they were requested to initiate legal action against the persons involved in forgery. The RAJUK also informed the matter to the CID on 22-2-1994. The RAJUK has been possessing the disputed property. The Rule should be discharged.

5. The High Court Division, by the impugned judgment and order, discharged the Rule. Then the appellants preferred appeal upon getting leave. One Aziz-al-Masud, claiming that the appellant had entered into an agreement for sale of the disputed property with him on 28-1-2007 and delivered possession of the same, thereby, he has acquired right in the property, in question. The RAJUK, violating the provision of law, evicted him from the disputed property. Thus, he filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2502 of 2013. This Division, without granting leave, tagged the said Civil Petition with the instant Civil Appeal for consideration.

6. Mr Kamal-ul-Alam and Mr AM Aminuddin, learned Senior Counsel appeared for the appellants. On the other hand, Mr Mahbubey Alam, learned Senior Counsel appeared for the RAJUK. Mr AM Aminuddin, learned Senior Counsel appeared on behalf of Aziz-al-Masud, the petitioner of Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2502 of 2013. Mr Mahbubey Alam, learned Senior Counsel appeared for the respondents in CP No. 2502 of 2013.

7. Learned Counsel for the appellants and the petitioner of Civil Petition submit that the High Court Division erred in law in failing to appreciate that title to the disputed property has been vested with the Ataul Huq since he got decree in a suit for specific performance of contract in respect of the disputed property against the RAJUK which was upheld up to the Appellate Division. They submit that it was the obligation of the RAJUK to mutate their names in its record. They further submit that Ataul Huq, predecessor-in-interest of the appellants, entered into an agreement to purchase the disputed property with the admitted owner and the RAJUK advised him to file a suit and filing suit he obtained decree which was upheld up to the Appellate Division and, thereafter, executing the said decree got the sale deed registered, thereby, acquired valid title and interest in the disputed property, the High Court Division erred in law in not directing the RAJUK to mutate the names of the writ-petitioner- appellants in its record.

8. Mr Mahbubey Alam, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the RAJUK, submits that the alleged agreement and decree on the basis of the said agreement and subsequent deed of KM Ataul Huq through Court are fraudulent and ineffective since the RAJUK cancelled the allotment of its allottee, namely, Mostafa Haider, so at the time of passing of decree in the suit for Specific Performance of Contract Mostafa Haider had no transferable interest in respect of his lease hold right in the disputed property and, thus, the decree and sale deed did not confer any title in favour of Maul Huq, it such view of the matter, the High Court Division rightly refused to direct the RAJUK to mutate the names of the writ-petitioners in its record. He submits that it is true that the suit for Specific Performance of Contract was decreed by the appellate Court but the same was hopelessly barred by limitation. He further submits that it is apparent on the face of the record that the signatures of Mostafa Haider appeared in the "baina nama" and application allegedly made by him to the RAJUK for according permission for selling the disputed property do not tally with those of his undisputed signature appeared in the lease deed i.e. the aforesaid decree was product of forgery and fraud.

9. Judicial review is a potent we open but the judge should know his limitations and the limitations of judicial process; and that the law cannot offer relief from "the heartache and thousand natural shocks that flesh is heir to" Article 102 of the Constitution confers jurisdiction of the writ Court to inquire into the controversy raised, it will exercise extra-ordinary power with utmost care, caution and circumspection keeping in view well recognised principles of law.

10. In this case admittedly, the disputed property originally belonged to RAJUK and it allotted the same to one Mostafa Haider by executing and registering a deed of lease dated 9-10-1965. It is the case of the writ-petitioners that Mostafa Haider executed an agreement for sale of the disputed property in favour of Ataul Huq, predecessor-in-interest of the appellants on 5-8-1971, that is, the same was alleged to have been executed during the war of liberation. It has been stated in the writ petition that Mostafa Haider himself on 6-8-1971 wrote a letter addressing the Chairman, DIT for according permission to sell the disputed property to KM Ataul Huq. The appellants produced a photo copy of the lease deed dated 9-10-1965 executed by the then DIT to Mostafa Haider, agreement for sale allegedly executed by Mostafa Haider in favour of KM Ataul Huq, dated 5-8-1971 and the application allegedly filed by Mostafa Haider addressing the Chairman DIT on 6-8-1971 seeking permission to sell the disputed land. The signatures of Mostafa Haider in those three documents are reproduced here:

11. If a prudent man compares the nature and shapes of the second two alleged signatures of Mostafa Haider those with his first undisputed signature he would definitely find the differences in those signatures. The appellants predecessor KM Ataul Huq managed to get decree in the suit for Specific Performance of Contract against Mostafa Haider claiming that second two signatures were the signatures of Mostafa Haider who admittedly put first signature of his lease deed.

12. It was the case of KM Ataul Huq, plaintiff in Title Suit No. 180 of 1975 that Mostafa Haider receiving rest consideration i.e. Taka 41,000 executed a sale deed in favour of KM Ataul Huq in December, 1971 but sale deed was not registered and, thus, KM Maul Huq filed the aforesaid suit for Specific Performance of Contract. First page of the said sale deed is reproduced here: 13. From the above first page it appears that the date and month of such execution are altered by pen through.

14. Mr Mahbubey Alam, learned Senior Counsel produced the note-sheet of the nothi of RAJUK in this Division. It appears from the noting dated 30-3-1972 of the nothi that, "অবস্থাদৃষ্টে মনে হয় জমির মালিক হায়দার একজন পশ্চিম পাকিস্তানি এবং একজন নিখোঁজ" It further appears from the "noting" on 23-4-1975 that, " NW(K) দাগের বরাদ্ধ গ্রহিতা জনাব মোস্তফা হায়দার দলিল মোতাবেক বাড়ী করিতে না পারায় কারণ দর্শানোর নোটিশ প্রদান করা হয়। বরাদ্দ গ্রহিতাকে তাহার ঠিকানায় না পাওয়ায় ডাক কর্তৃপক্ষ not known সই করা সমন নোটিশ ফেরত পাঠাইয়া দিয়াছেন। অবগতি ও পরবর্তী ব্যবস্থার জন্য নথি পেশ করা হইল।" On 3-5-1975 it was noted that "উক্ত প্লটটিকে abandoned property হিসাবে লিস্টভুক্ত করা যাইতে পারে এবং প্রয়োজনীয় ব্যবস্থা করা যাইতে পারে।” On 22-5-1975 it was noted that “মাননীয় চেয়ারম্যান সাহেবের উপরোক্ত নির্দেশনা অনুসারে প্লট নং NW(K)II abandoned property অর্ন্তভুক্ত। কাজেউ অনুমোদনের জন্য তাহার নিকট পাঠান যাইতে পারে। Thereafter, on 25-5-1975, it was noted that, “পূর্ব পৃষ্ঠার আদেশ মোতাবেক বরাদ্দ বাতিল করার জন্য পেশ করা হইল।” In noting No. 25 dated 28-2-1977 it was stated, “ট্রাস্টি বোর্ড বিগত ১৯৬তম সাধারণ সভায় এন ডব্লিউ(ক) ১১নং প্লটের বরাদ্দ বাতিলের অন্যান্য প্লটের বরাদ্দ বাতিলের সহিত অনুমোদন করিয়াছেন। অতএব, এনই(ডি)৫নং প্লটের নথিতে মাননীয় চেয়ারম্যান সাহেবের আদেশ অনুসারে ইহার ফেরত দখল বুঝিয়া নিবার জন্য সংশ্লিষ্ট বিঃপ্রাঃ অনুরোধ করা যাইতে পারে।” Possession of the disputed property was taken over by the RAJUK on 29-6-1977.

15. The appellants produced a certificate issued by Dr Kamal Hossain, a Senior Advocate of this Court and Chairman of the constitution draft committee. The contents of the said certificate were as follows: "TO WHOM IT MAY CONCERN It has been brought to my attention that some person has been impersonating my late cousin Mostafa Haider, son of late Khandaker Fazle Haider (eldest brother of my mother). Mostafa Haider died in Karachi at age of 66 years due to cardiac arrest on 26 May, 2003. Any person claiming, to be Mostafa Haider is an importer, who is fraudulently seeking to pass himself off as Mostafa Haider for a manifestly ulterior purpose which renders him liable to be criminally prosecuted. Kamal Hossain"

16. In the written statement filed by the RAJUK it was categorically contended, "that the suit land has been declared as abandoned under Memo No. DIT/EO(N)2517-L dated 29-5-1975, as such, the suit is not maintainable". While passing decree in the suit for specific performance of contract, the Courts did not at all consider and determine the point as to whether the disputed property is abandoned property or not.

17. It appears from the judgment of the Title Suit No. 180 of 1975 that it was dismissed by the trial Court mainly on the ground that the same was barred by limitation.

18. The trial Court, in it judgment observed that "the defendant No. 1 (Mostafa Haider) would execute and register the requisite sale deed within 6(six) months from the date of execution from Exhibit-2 i.e. within 6(six) months from 5th day of August, 1971 but the suit was filed on 19-3-1975 according to the provision of Article 113 of the Limitation Act, 1908 the instant suit ought to have been filed within 3 (three) years from date fixed for performance of contract i.e. within 4th day of February 1975. So the suit is filed beyond the statutory period of limitation. In such view of the matter, I hold that the suit is barred by limitation and, as such, it is not maintainable." The appellate Court in Title Appeal No. 51 of 1989 reversed the said finding with the following observations: “ইহা স্বীকৃত ও এগ্রিমেন্ট (প্রদর্শনী-২) হারা প্রমাণিত যে, ৫-৮-৭১ ইং তারিখে চুক্তি নামটি সম্পাদিত হয় এবং চুক্তির নামার শর্ত থাকে যে, ১নং বিবাদী চুক্তি নামার তারিখ হইতে ৬ মাসের মধ্যে প্রয়োজনীয় ডিক্রি কবলা সম্পাদন ও রেজিস্ট্রি করিয়া দিবে। হ্হা স্বীকৃত যে, বাদী পক্ষ চুক্তি প্রবলে কবলা পাওয়ার নিমিত্তে ১৯-৩-৭৫ তারিখে মামলা দায়ের করেন। বিজ্ঞ নিম্নআদালত অভিমত পোষন করেন যে, আইনের বিধান অনুযায়ী অর্থাৎ ৪-২-৭৫ ইং তারিখের মধ্যে মামলাটি দায়ের করিতে পারেন নাই বিধায় বাদীর মামলা তামাদিতে বারিত। আলোচ্য ক্ষেত্রে ১ মাস ১৫ দিনের তামাদি গণ্য করতঃ বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত ১ ও ২ নং বিচার্ধ্য বিষয় এর সিদ্ধান্ত বাদীর প্রতিকুলে সাব্যস্থা করিয়াছেন । এই পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে আপীলকারীর নিযুক্তীয় বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবী যুক্তি প্রদর্শন করতঃ বলেন যে, পিও ১২/৭২ এর ৪ ধারা উপেক্ষা করিয়া রায় প্রদান করিয়াছেন বিধায় মূল মামলার রায়টি বাদীর অনুকূলে যায় নাই । এই পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে আপীলকারীর নিযুক্তীয় বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবী উক্ত পিও ১২/৭২ এর বিধানটি উল্লেখ করেন । সঠিক অনুধাবনের জন্য উহা নিম্নে প্রদত্ত হইলঃ-

Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for time being in force, in computing the period of limitation prescribed for any legal proceeding by or under any law, the period between the 1st day of March, 1971 and the 1st day of March, 1972 (both days inclusive) shall be excluded. আপীলকারীর নিযুক্তীয় বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবীর উক্তি যুক্তি প্রদর্শনের পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে রেসপনডেন্ট পক্ষের নিযুক্তীয় বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবী পাল্টা বক্তব্য আদালতে পেশ করিতে স্বত্ববান ও সমর্থ হন নাই। এক্ষেত্রে আগীলকারীর নিষুক্তীয় বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবীর বক্তব্যের মধ্যে যথেষ্ট সারবস্তা আছে বলিয়া আমি অভিমত পোষন করি । আপীলকারীর নিযুক্তীয় বিজ্ঞ আইনজীবী উত্থাপিত পিও ১২/৭২ এর বিধানটি পর্যালোচনা করিলে বাদী পক্ষের মামলা তামাদিতে আখ্যায়িত করিবার মত কোন কারণ আছে বলিয়া আদালত মনে করেন না।”

19 The High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2559 of 1992 affirmed the said finding with the following observations: "The period of limitation in filing the suit for Specific Performance of Contract, limitation is 3 years and the suit having been filed on 19-3-1975 and the cause of action arose in 1971 and in view of Article 4 of PO 12 of 1972 which exclude the period of limitation in between the 1st day of March, 1971 and the 1st day March, 1972, the plaintiff opposite party is very much within time."

20. PO 12 of 1972 provides that the period between the 1st day of March, 1971 and the 1st day of March, 1972 (both days inclusive) shall be excluded in computing the period of limitation prescribed for any legal proceeding by or under any law. Both the appellate Court and revisional Court discussed the matter but curiously held that the suit was not barred by limitation.

21. We have seen that the agreement for sale was allegedly executed on 5-8-1971 i.e. the plaintiff was entitled to get benefit of said computation of the period of limitation but definitely such limitation started to run on and from first day March 1972, and the plaintiff was entitled to get three years time to file the instant suit as per provision of Article 113 of the Limitation Act, that is, he had to file suit on or before 1-3-1975 but the same was filed on 19-3-1975. The courts below discussed the matter but erroneously held that the suit was not barred by limitation inasmuch as the same was filed after 18 days of the stipulated period of limitation in view of the provisions of PO 12 of 1972 and Article 113 of the Limitation Act.

22. Curious enough is that the RAJUK preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal producing a certified copy of the judgment and order of the High Court Division which was not genuine. Accordingly, Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 788 of 2004 was dismissed and this Division directed the Registrar to hold inquiry over the matter.

23. The contents of the said order dated 4-5-2006 of this Division run as follows:- "Date of hearing: The 4th May, 2006. ORDER We have heard the learned Counsel of both the parties at length. The leave petition is barred by 136 days. Further more the Civil Petition has not been accompanied by genuine certified copy of the impugned order of the High Court Division and, as such, the leave petition being not in form is dismissed. It appears that the petitioner has annexed a certified copy of the impugned order which is different from that furnished by Mr TH Khan, the learned Counsel of the respondents. The said copy be kept with the record. The registrar is therefore directed to enquire into the matter as to how two certified copies of the same judgment of the High Court Division dated 23-6-2003 could be different and fix up responsibility of the person/persons. The inquiry report is to be submitted by 21st May, 2006. Sd/-Syed JR Mudassir Husain, CJ Sd/-MM Ruhul Amin, J Sd/-Amirul Kabir Chowdhury, J The 4th May, 2006"

24. The RAJUK filed Civil Review Petition No. 51 of 2007 for reviewing the order passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 788 of 2004. Said review petition was dismissed.

25. The contents of the said order dated 6-8-2007 run as follows: "Date of hearing: The 6th August, 2007. ORDER The Review Petition has been filed against the judgment dated May 04, 2007 passed in Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No.788 of 2004 dismissing the same being barred by limitation and leave petition was not in form and present Review Petition also barred by 02 days. We have perused the materials on record and we do not find any ground to review our order sought to be reviewed. Accordingly, the review petition is dismissed. Sd/-Md Ruhul Amin, CJ Sd/-M Fazlul Karim, J Sd/-MM Ruhul Amin, J Sd/-T Islam, J Sd/-Md Joynul Abedin, J Sd/-Hassan Ameen, J" The 6th August, 2007"

26. Those are the activities of the officials of the RAJUK to conduct the case.

27. It further appears from the materials on record that the appellants produced a certificate issued by a Sub Divisional Officer, Sadar (South) Dhaka dated 27-10-1971 in Title Suit No. 459 of 1985 wherein it was stated that the disputed property is not an abandoned property. That certificate was marked as exhibit-8 to the said suit. Relying upon which, the said suit for Specific Performance of Contract was decreed by the appellate Court. Interesting aspect is that the law relating to abandoned property, that is, the Bangladesh Abandoned Property (Control, Management and Dismissal) Order 1972 (PO 16 of 1972) came into force on 28-2-1972 but the Sub Divisional Officer issued the aforesaid certificate that the disputed property is not abandoned property on 27-10-1971, that is, before enactment of the law said certificate was allegedly issued. It is to be mentioned here that the RAJUK in its written statement in the said suit stated that the suit property is abandoned property.

28. The contents of the certificate allegedly issued by the Sub Divisional Officer, Sadar (South) dated 27-10-1971 run as follows: "Government of East Pakistan, Office of the Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (South), Dacca. This is to certify that the immovable property as per scheduled below is not an abandoned property or has not been restored within one year of the issuance of this certificate. Schedule 1. Measurement of plot- 2. Situation—One bigha and eight Chattak in Gulshan Model Town, DIT, in sub-Registrar's office at Dacca, Mouja, Bhola Shamair, RS. Tejgaon, District-Dacca. 3. Number of plot and block-at plot No. 11NW(K) bearing holding No.50, Gulshan Residential Area, Dacca. MA Hye Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (South), Dacca. Memo No. 8289 Y(en) Dated 27-10-71 copy forwarded to— (1)The District Registrar, Dacca (2)Mostafa Haider for information and necessary action. Sd/- Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (South), Dacca, 27-10-71 "

29. Aforesaid certificate, on the face of it, was a fraudulent document. We take this opportunity to record our strong and empathetic disapproval of the conduct of Ataul Huq, predecessor-in-interest of the appellants.

30. On 15-3-1972, that is, after independence, KM Ataul Huq filed an application addressing the Chairman, DIT for getting allotment of the disputed plot. Contents of the said application run as follows:— "The Chairman, Dacca Improvement Trust, Dacca. Dear Sir, Re: Plot No. NWK(II) Road No. 50, Gulshan Residential Area, Dacca. I have the honour to bring to your kind notice that the Lessee of the aforesaid Gulshan Plot Mr Mostafa Haider agreed to sell the said plot and applied to your honour on 6th August, 1971 (copy enclosed), Accordingly I seek your permission to issue necessary orders to enable me to purchase the plot vide my letter dated 6th August, 1971 (copy enclosed). You issued a letter No. DIT/EO/1006 dated 14-9-71 to Mr Mostafa Haider (copy enclosed) under copy to me and asked to fulfil certain conditions for approval. In compliance to your said letter of 14-9-1971. I executed an agreement (Annexure-A) with the DIT on Rs. 1/50 stamp paper on 14-9-71 and also I agreed to fulfil other conditions as laid down in the said letter. You very kindly accorded permission of transfer of the property vide your Memo No. DIT/ EC /1102 dated 27-9-71 (copy enclosed). On receipt of your kind permission for transfer of the plot Mr Mostafa Haider handed over original lease Deed between DIT and Mr Haider and other connecting papers and I incurred the following amounts. 1) In compliance to your Memo No DIT/EO/2761 dated 20-6-70 Interest for delayed payment of 2nd, 3rd and 4th instalments amounting to Rs. 657.75 paid to DIT's A/C with National Bank vide credit adice No. 178 dt. 7-9-71 by me. 2) Paid to Mr Mostafa Haider, the lessor an amount of Rs. 11,000 at advance money. 3) Purchased stamp paper for sale deed worth Rs. 3,020 vide Dacca Treasury Chalan No. A/8, dated 27-10-71. 4) Obtained certificate from SDO (South) Dacca on 27-10-71 to the effect that the property is not abandoned for registering the sale deed. In order to register the plot all formalities such as Income Tax Clearance Certificate etc. were being made by Mr Haider and in the meantime the war began and registration of the transfer deed could not be made. It may not be out of place to mention here that I have no residential house or any plot in my name or in the name of my wife or dependents in Dacca or elsewhere in Bangladesh. I suffered such during the last liberation movement. Considering the above circumstances and the money I have invested for transfer of the above plot in my name, I would request you to be kind enough to allot me the aforesaid plot for which act of kindness I shall remain grateful to you for ever. Thanking you. Yours faithfully, (KM Ataul Huq) Manager National Insurance Co. of Bangladesh Ltd."

31. From the said letter it appears that KM Ataul Huq stated that he had paid Rs. 11,000 to Mostafa Haider as advance money. He stated that he had purchased stamp paper for sale deed worth of Rs.3,020 but he did not state anything about execution of sale deed alleged to have been executed by Mostafa Haider in his favour in the month of December, 1971. In the so id application he further stated he had paid Rs. 11,000 but in the unregistered deed of sale alleged to have been executed in December, 1971 he stated that he had paid entire consideration, that is, Rs. 52,000.

32. Upon careful examination of all those documents and stated facts and circumstances, it is apparent that the plaintiff somehow managed the decree for Specific Performance of Contract. There is no finding of either of courts in respect of the claim of the RAJUK as to abandoned character of the disputed property and as to the consequence of taking loan from IFIC bank by Mostafa Haider mortgaging disputed property in the bank. Subsequently, IFIC bank went on liquidation.

33. It appears from the facts and circumstances that some actions taken by the officials of the RAJUK are highly questionable which are apparent from the letter issued by it directing Ataul Huq to file suit. It was not the duty of the officials of the RAJUK to advise any one to file suit against the RAJUK which is highly deprecated. The actions of the RAJUK officials in filing a civil petition and a review petition in the Appellate Division by producing in genuine copy of the judgment of the High Court Division passed in Civil Revision No. 2559 of 1992. It was the duty of the RAJUK to hold enquiry and to find out the person/ persons who were involved in those malafide activities and to take steps accordingly.

34. Another aspect is that the RAJUK cancelled the allotment of Mostafa Haider on 29-5-1975 i.e. at the time of passing decree Mostafa Haider lost his leasehold right in the disputed property. The RAJUK was not a party to the alleged agreement for sale. So by obtaining decree of Specific Performance of Contract against Mostafa Haider and getting sale deed through Court, Ataul Huq, predecessor-in-interest of the appellants acquired any valid title or not is a debatable question. Though in its judgment passed in Title Suit No. 559 of 1985, the trial Court observed that such cancellation of lease was effected during pendency of the suit but in a suit for Specific Performance of Contract, the court cannot declare that the cancellation of an instrument was void. It is to be mentioned here that the contract between Mostafa Haider and the DIT was terminable contract since the same contains an stipulation that in certain event it may be put an end to. At the relevant time, Ataul Huq was third party since he did not acquire any right or title in the disputed property at that time. In order to get decree for declaration that cancellation of an instrument void, the person having right in the property should challenge the order of cancellation in an appropriate forum and in a legally permissible process.

35. In the instant writ petition, the writ-petitioner appellants have prayed for a direction to mutate their names in the record of the RAJUK. Admittedly, the RAJUK cancelled lease of Mostafa Haider, with whom Ataul Huq allegedly made agreement to purchase his lease hold right. Until order of cancellation of lease of Mostafa Haider is declared void or illegal by a competent court following legally approved process, it is difficult to hold that order of cancellation of lease-deed lost its efficacy and the appellants acquired any valid right in the disputed property through Mostafa Haider.

36. It is relevant here to state that when one of the parties to a suit or other proceeding tenders, or has put in evidence, a judgment, order or decree it is open to the party against whom it is offered to avoid its effect on the ground that the judgment was obtained through fraud. A fraudulent judgment and decree may be avoided in the proceedings in which it is sought to be relied upon. It is not necessary to have it set-aside by instituting independent proceedings in a competent Court. A judgment or decree obtained by practicing fraud upon a Court binds no such Court or any one else claiming through such judgment or decree though it has not been set-aside or reversed.

37. From the aforesaid facts and circumstances, it appears that in this case complex question of facts is involved and matter requires through probe on facts and the question of title, after cancellation of lease deed, is disputed so the writ-petitioners were not entitled to get relief in writ jurisdiction.

38. Moreover, the jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution is extra-ordinary equitable and discretionary. Prerogative writs mentioned therein may be issued for doing substantial justice. It is, therefore, of utmost necessity that writ-petitioner approaching the writ Court must come with clean hands. While exercising the extra-ordinary power a writ court would certainly bear in mind the conduct of the party who invokes the jurisdiction of the Court. The writ-petitioner must disclose all material facts without any reservation even if they are against him. Where the source of the right is rooted in fraud or established dubious considerations, no right stricto sensu for implementation could arise and for less enforceable by way of mandamus in the writ jurisdiction.

39. From the process adopted by Ataul Huq, which is apparent from the discussion made above, to get decree and transfer deed registered through court, we have to hesitation to hold that his hands are not clean. A writ of mandamus is controlled by equitable principles and can be issued only in favour of a person who comes to the court with clean hands and who is not guilty of fraud or bad faith in respect of the matters in controversy between the parties. It will not be granted where more harm than good will result from its issuance.

40. In view of the facts and circumstances stated above, this is to observe that the. High Court Division rightly refused to exercise its extra-ordinary jurisdiction in the instant writ petition.

Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed. The Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal is also dismissed.

End.
